clue.text: German admitting the object is sex

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word for German takes something inside it

blocks.note: an end is an object or aim, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about how a German noun's object relates to its sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests German grammar, where nouns have genders; 'object' really means an aim, as in 'to that end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is used as a synonym for whether a person or creature is male or female.

clue.text: Tremendous one-night show caps singular buffoonery

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece caps another by sitting on top of it, so the show comes first

blocks.note: a gig is a single performance by a band
antics are buffoonery; the singular form drops the final S

explanation.surface: A one-off comedy show topping a run of clownish behaviour, sounding like a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' is the instruction to take the one-item form of antics.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size or scale, so they are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Eye problem leaves listeners in the dark

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it goes inside the second word

blocks.note: ears are what we listen with
night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: Someone's poor eyesight means the audience is left in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb about the audience but only joins definition to wordplay, in the sense of 'results in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Near sight, usually called short sight or myopia, is the condition of seeing close things clearly but distant ones blurrily.

clue.text: It's bad to be climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A warning that clambering up somewhere is a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be' looks like part of the grammar, but it is the verb 'exist', written backwards up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means morally wicked, which is one strong sense of the adjective bad.

clue.text: 19's arrangement for providing support for the retired

indicators.note: an arrangement of something puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Some cleverly arranged scheme supporting pensioners in their old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The retired' sounds like pensioners, but means people who have gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is what holds up a sleeper's body once they have gone to bed for the night.

clue.text: Sick painter inhales oxygen and dangerous drug

indicators.note: a sick painter is in a bad state, so the word is broken up and rearranged
to inhale is to take in, so the jumbled word draws the extra letter inside

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An ill artist breathing oxygen alongside a dangerous drug, like a hospital scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a poisonous alkaloid from deadly nightshade, used medically to dilate pupils, so it is a hazardous drug.

clue.text: Scruffy old woman under paper creating temporal diversion

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece under another sits below it, so the paper goes first

blocks.note: The Times is a London newspaper
a witch, informally, is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: A shabby old woman sitting beneath a newspaper, causing a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diversion' is read as a switch that turns a current one way or another, controlled by a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A time switch is a clock-operated device that changes an electrical circuit at set hours, a switch governed by the time.

clue.text: Daughter of Zeus in danger at Olympic Games

indicators.note: the answer is said to be in the following words, lying inside them across the gaps

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of danger, all of at and the start of Olympic

explanation.surface: Mythology meets sport: a goddess facing peril at the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympic fits Zeus on Mount Olympus, which hides the device.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato, Muse of lyric and love poetry, was one of the nine Muses, children of Zeus and Mnemosyne.

clue.text: Material noticed clothing a model

indicators.note: clothing something wraps around it, so one word goes outside the other

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Fabric spotted dressing a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests the catwalk, but it is the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Sateen is a glossy cotton fabric woven to imitate satin, so it is a material or cloth.

clue.text: Angry plagiarist losing patience, initially

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word
initially points to only the first letter of patience being the part removed

blocks.note: a pirate copies others' work, as a plagiarist does

explanation.surface: Someone who copies other people's work gets cross and loses their patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym of furious or cross, describing someone in a temper.

clue.text: Worker is less industrious after final warning

indicators.note: final asks for the last letter only of the following word
one piece placed after another comes second in the line

explanation.surface: An employee slacks off after being given a final warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final warning' looks like a disciplinary step, but it asks only for the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a tradesman who fits glass into windows, so a specific kind of craftsman or labourer.

clue.text: Unrestrained politician one involved in tirade

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

explanation.surface: A politician caught up in a furious tirade, out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant describes something spreading or growing wildly without check, which matches being uncontrolled.

clue.text: Retreat, being snared originally in trap

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the opening letter of snared counts
one thing in another goes inside it

explanation.surface: Running away but being caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest, in the sense of a snug hideaway or den, is a private retreat where one can shelter.

clue.text: Debark tree after short letter received in shop

indicators.note: the tree comes after the other piece in the line
something received in a place is taken inside it

blocks.note: Ep. is the short form of epistle, a letter

explanation.surface: Stripping a tree after a brief note arrives at the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debark' suggests removing bark from a tree; here it means to leave a ship. Ep. is the abbreviation for epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: To debark is to disembark, leaving a ship and going on land.

clue.text: County is to engage supporting bowlers from overseas

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece is held up underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: Americans call a bowler hat a derby
to engage staff is to hire them

explanation.surface: A county cricket club plans to sign up foreign bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowlers' suggests cricketers, which fits a county side, but they are hats; a bowler is a round hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Derbyshire is an English county in the East Midlands, home of the Peak District.

clue.text: Singer distracted painter

indicators.note: a distracted mind is scattered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A vocalist whose attention keeps wandering to an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical artist famous for portraits and nudes.

clue.text: Well-liked Communist leader is a non-believer

explanation.surface: A popular Communist leader turns out to have no religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communist leader' looks like a first-letter instruction; it is Fidel Castro.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is someone without faith, especially one rejecting a particular religion.

clue.text: The conductor, freshly chosen, travelled below

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed below comes after the other

blocks.note: elect after a title means newly chosen, as in president-elect
rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A newly appointed orchestra conductor who travelled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests music or a bus; here it carries electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal through which electric current enters or leaves a circuit, a conductor of electricity.

clue.text: Doughty fellow has no appreciation of music

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
having no ear for music is to be earless

explanation.surface: A brave man who happens to be tone-deaf.
explanation.walkthrough: To have an ear for music is to appreciate it, so without one you are earless.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughty is an old-fashioned word for brave and resolute, matching the sense of having no fear.

clue.text: Most astute males rise above examination

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards
in a down clue the piece above comes first

explanation.surface: The cleverest men come out on top in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Males' sounds like men in general; it is the male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartest is the superlative of smart, meaning clever or quick-witted, just as astute is.

clue.text: Injured strikers returning to bed

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: Footballers who got hurt go back to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' suggests football forwards; they are bats that hit a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabbed means wounded with a knife or sharp point, a particular way of being hurt.

clue.text: Cry from son getting ointment

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy yells as ointment is rubbed on his graze.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud, piercing shout of fear or pain, so it is a type of yell.

clue.text: Accent producing mutual confusion

indicators.note: confusion mixes things up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A strong regional accent leaves two speakers baffling each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accent' suggests speech, but it is the written mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the two-dot diacritic placed over vowels in German, a written accent mark.

clue.text: The way to capture Conservative area

indicators.note: capturing something takes it prisoner, holding it inside

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Election tactics: the route to winning a Tory-held district.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a small piece of ground, or someone's territory or beat, so it is a region.

clue.text: Intends catching redhead in wood, showing bad trait

indicators.note: catching something holds it, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: the head, first letter, of red

explanation.surface: Someone plans to catch a red-haired person hiding in the woods, revealing their nasty side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' looks like a ginger person; it is the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean streak is a vein of unkindness in someone's character, an unpleasant characteristic.

clue.text: Smell a foreign city the foreign way

blocks.note: Rome as the Italians write it

explanation.surface: A traveller sniffs a city abroad the way locals do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The foreign way' asks for the city's name in its own language, not English.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive, usually pleasant odour, which is a kind of scent.

clue.text: Teacher has time in jail

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one word holds another inside

blocks.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster serving a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time in jail' reads as a prison sentence; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, so it means a gaol in crossword and criminal parlance.

clue.text: Cut bread when rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: Slicing bread once it has risen in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' fits dough, but it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore or rebuff them pointedly, the same as to snub them.

clue.text: Give protection currently to a feature about princess

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a nose is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Guarding a princess's appearance, like a bodyguard or image consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' seems to mean now; it means by electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: To anodise is to coat metal with a protective oxide layer by electrolysis, using an electrical charge.

clue.text: Forgive prisoner? That's acceptable!

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to pardon an inmate, and the answer is a clear yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or excuse wrongdoing, accepting it instead of punishing it.

clue.text: Reject paintings and poetry being cross

indicators.note: rejecting something sends it back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: An angry critic dismissing pictures and poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the verb, to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel over or through an area, so it means to go across it.

clue.text: Bishop despatched after a truant

indicators.note: the pieces come after the article in the line

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is sent off to chase a pupil skipping school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truant' looks like a noun; here it is the adjective, missing from school.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant pupil is away from school without permission, so they are not present.
